summary: Adolf Friedrich Stenzler was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Berlin, Greifswald, Bonn, and Paris under Bopp, Schlegel, and Lassen. He became Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Breslau in 1833 and Wrocław University Library sub-librarian (1834–1872).

Adolf Holtzmann the Elder was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Othmar Frank, Johann Andreas Schmeller, and Eugène Burnouf. From 1852 to 1870, he served as Professor of German Literature and Sanskrit at Heidelberg University.
Adolf Kaegi was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied under Rudolf von Roth around 1872–1874. He served as a professor at the University of Zurich from approximately 1883 to 1914.

Adolf Kirchhoff was a scholar of linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at the Humboldt University of Berlin (~1842–1846) and later held a post there and at Frederick William University Berlin (~1865–1908).

Adolphe Régnier was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Eugène Burnouf (~1838–1844). He held posts at the Palace of Fontainebleau and served as Professor of Latin Eloquence at the Collège de France (~1857–1864).

Adrian Zenz is a scholar of Tibetology and Sinology. He studied at the University of Auckland and completed his PhD at the University of Cambridge under Hildegard Diemberger. He held posts at Columbia International University Korntal and the Victims of Communism Memorial Foundation.

Agata Bareja-Starzyńska works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She conducted research at the University of Oslo (1993) and the University of Bonn (1995), and held a post at the University of Warsaw (attested 2008).

Agathon Benary was a linguist who studied at Göttingen, Halle-Wittenberg, and under Franz Bopp. He held professorships at Köllnisches Gymnasium and Humboldt University of Berlin from around 1833 to 1860.

Agehananda Bharati was a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Vienna. He held posts at Banaras Hindu University, Delhi, Tokyo, Kyoto, the University of Washington, and Syracuse University (professor of anthropology, 1961–1991).

Agnieszka Helman-Ważny is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. She studied at the Academy of Fine Arts, Warsaw, and earned her PhD at Nicolaus Copernicus University in Toruń. She held posts at Cornell University (~2008–2010) and the University of Warsaw (2015).

Ahmad Hasan Dani was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Banaras Hindu University and the University of London under Altekar, Wheeler, and Codrington. He held posts at Dhaka, Peshawar, SOAS, and Quaid-i-Azam University.

Ajahn Amaro is a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Bedford College and under Ajahn Chah and Ajahn Sumedho. He co-founded and served as co-abbot of Abhayagiri Buddhist Monastery (~1996–2010) and became Abbot of Amaravati Buddhist Monastery around 2010.
Ajahn Brahm is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Cambridge, including Emmanuel College (~1969–1972), and trained under Boonman Poonyathiro (~1970–1974).
Ajit Ranjan Bhattacharyya, an Indologist and scholar of Buddhist studies, studied under Vidhusekhara Bhattacharya. He held a post at the University of Calcutta as an Ex-Puranchand Nahar Fellow.

Akifumi Naito is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University and under Gadjin Nagao. He held posts at the Research Institute of Shin Buddhism, Ryukoku University, Kyoto Women's University, and Gyoshin Buddhist Academy.

Akihiko Akamatsu is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. He studied at Kyoto University and earned a PhD from the University of Paris/Sorbonne Nouvelle. He held academic posts at Kyoto University and was Associate Professor at Kyushu University.
Akihiro Oda is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied at Otani University. He later held posts there as a full-time lecturer (attested 1992) and Professor of Buddhist Studies (attested 2013).

Akiko Walley is a scholar of Japanology, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Aoyama Gakuin University (~1994–2001) and Harvard University (~2001–2009), and held a post at the University of Oregon (2009–2016).

Akimichi Eda is an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Dr. phil. from the University of Marburg (attested 2005). Eda studied under Katsumi Mimaki, Khangkar Tsultrim Kelsang, and doctoral supervisor Michael Hahn.
Akio Donohashi is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1968–1976) and served as a professor at Kobe University (~1989–2012).
